title: Do EU transport operators have to train drivers on tachograph use?
description: Regulation (EU) 165/2014 Article 33: the operator's duty to train and instruct drivers on tachographs, regular checks, record retention and liability.
shortAnswer: Yes. Article 33(1) of Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 makes transport undertakings responsible for ensuring that their drivers are properly trained and instructed on the correct functioning of digital and analogue tachographs, for making regular checks that drivers use them correctly, and for not giving incentives that encourage misuse. Undertakings are liable for their drivers' infringements, and Member States may make that liability conditional on a breach of the training and checking duty.
keyTakeaways: Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 on tachographs applies from 2 March 2016 and has been amended by Regulation (EU) 2020/1054 and Regulation (EU) 2024/1230.

Article 33(1) requires transport undertakings to train and instruct drivers on tachographs, check their use regularly, and avoid incentives to misuse; Article 10(2) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 adds a duty to properly instruct drivers on driving time rules.
Drivers must be able to produce records for the current day and the preceding 56 days at a roadside check (Article 36), and must record border crossings (Article 34).
Undertakings must keep record sheets and printouts for at least a year (Article 33(2)) and keep downloaded digital data for at least 12 months (Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, Article 10(5)).
Under Article 33(3), undertakings are liable for drivers' infringements; Member States may make that liability conditional on the undertaking breaching its training and checking duty.
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; directly applicable regulation with EEA relevance)
regulator: European Parliament and Council of the European Union through Regulation (EU) No 165/2014, enforced by each Member State's road transport control authorities
appliesTo: Road transport undertakings operating vehicles within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006
Drivers of goods and passenger vehicles fitted with analogue, digital or smart tachographs
Transport managers and compliance staff who analyze tachograph data
Driver employment agencies supplying drivers to undertakings

sections.heading: What does Article 33 of Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 require?

blocks.text: Article 33(1) creates a three part duty for transport undertakings. In the words of the [consolidated Regulation (EU) No 165/2014](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R0165-20241231), they "shall be responsible for ensuring that their drivers are properly trained and instructed as regards the correct functioning of tachographs, whether digital or analogue, shall make regular checks to ensure that their drivers make correct use thereof, and shall not give to their drivers any direct or indirect incentives that could encourage the misuse of tachographs."

items: **Train and instruct:** cover the tachograph types actually fitted in the fleet. A driver trained only on analogue equipment is not properly trained for a smart tachograph.
**Check regularly:** the regulation does not set an interval, so the undertaking must define one and show that checks happen.

**No incentives to misuse:** pay and bonus structures are part of compliance. Article 10(1) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 separately bans payments linked to distance, delivery speed or load where they endanger road safety or encourage infringements.

blocks.text: Article 33(1) also requires undertakings to issue enough approved record sheets to drivers of analogue vehicles, and requires the undertaking and the driver of a digital tachograph vehicle to ensure that printouts can be made correctly if a control officer asks for them.

sections.heading: Which vehicles and undertakings are covered?

blocks.text: The duty applies wherever a tachograph is required. Article 3(1) requires tachographs in vehicles registered in a Member State used for the carriage of passengers or goods by road to which [Regulation (EC) No 561/2006](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02006R0561-20241231) on driving times and rest periods applies.

Member States may exempt vehicles listed in Article 13(1) and (3) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 and operations granted exceptions under its Article 14 (Article 3(2) and (3)). They may also require tachographs in other vehicles for national operations (Article 3(5)). The regulation was signed on 4 February 2014 and, under Article 48, applies from 2 March 2016, with Articles 24, 34 and 45 applying from 2 March 2015.

Equipment is changing, which changes the training content. Article 3(4) and (4a), inserted by Regulation (EU) 2020/1054, require vehicles operating in a Member State other than their Member State of registration to be fitted with the second version smart tachograph within set periods after the detailed technical provisions entered into force. Training should follow the equipment actually in each vehicle.

sections.heading: Which driver duties should tachograph training cover?

blocks.text: Training should cover every duty the regulation places on drivers, because Article 33(3) links the undertaking's liability to those duties. The main ones are in Articles 32, 34, 35 and 36.

blocks.text: The 56 day period was extended from 28 days by Regulation (EU) 2020/1054. Training materials written before that amendment, and before the border crossing entry rule, are a common source of outdated content. A periodic check for [outdated training content](/guides/how-to-detect-outdated-training-content) should include these two points.

sections.heading: What records must the undertaking keep?

blocks.text: Undertakings must keep tachograph records and make them available to drivers and control officers. Article 33(2) requires record sheets and printouts made under Article 35 to be kept in chronological order and legible form for at least a year after use, with copies given to drivers who ask.

items: Undertakings must give drivers who ask copies of data downloaded from their driver cards, together with printed versions (Article 33(2)).
Record sheets, printouts and downloaded data must be produced or handed over at the request of any authorized control officer (Article 33(2)).

Under Article 10(5) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, undertakings using digital recording equipment must download data from the vehicle unit and driver card as regularly as the Member State stipulates, and keep downloaded data for at least 12 months following recording, accessible from the undertaking's premises on request.
Driver cards are issued by the Member State of normal residence within one month of a complete application, and are valid for no more than five years (Article 26).

blocks.title: Training records are not specified
blocks.text: Neither Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 nor Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 sets a retention period for training records. Because Article 33(3) allows liability to turn on whether the undertaking met its training and checking duty, records of who was trained, on which equipment, and what each check found are the undertaking's main defense. See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: How does liability for driver infringements work?

blocks.text: Under Article 33(3), transport undertakings are liable for infringements of the regulation committed by their drivers or drivers at their disposal. Member States may make that liability conditional on the undertaking infringing the first subparagraph of Article 33(1), the training, checking and incentives duty, and Article 10(1) and (2) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006.

Article 10(2) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 requires the undertaking to organize drivers' work so they can comply, to "properly instruct the driver" and to make regular checks. Article 41 of Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 requires Member States to set penalties that are effective, proportionate, dissuasive and non-discriminatory, in line with the infringement categories in Directive 2006/22/EC. Penalty levels are national.

sections.heading: How does this relate to Driver CPC training?

blocks.text: Article 33 training is an employer duty that applies whenever a driver uses a tachograph, separate from the Certificate of Professional Competence. The CPC subject list in Annex I to Directive (EU) 2022/2561 includes tachograph use under Regulation (EU) No 165/2014, as covered on the [EU Driver CPC periodic training](/regulations/eu-driver-cpc-periodic-training) page, but a CPC course chosen by the driver does not show that the employer trained them on its own equipment and procedures.

As at November 2026, the consolidated text on EUR-Lex incorporates amendments up to 31 December 2024, including Regulation (EU) 2024/1230. Operators should confirm national download intervals and penalty rules with the control authority in each country of operation.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry turns each driver duty in Articles 32 to 36 into a defined knowledge point tied to the tachograph versions in the fleet, so training records show what each driver was taught and on which equipment. When a rule such as the 56 day period changes, the affected points and every course that uses them are flagged for update.

faqs.q: How often must tachograph training be repeated?
faqs.a: Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 does not set an interval. Article 33(1) requires drivers to be properly trained and instructed and checked regularly, so the undertaking should retrain when equipment changes, when rules change, and when its checks show errors, and should record why its chosen interval is adequate.

faqs.q: Does Article 33 apply to agency drivers?
faqs.a: Article 33(3) makes undertakings liable for infringements by their drivers or by drivers at their disposal, which includes drivers supplied by agencies. The undertaking should verify agency drivers' tachograph training before use and include them in its regular checks, since its liability can depend on those duties.

faqs.q: How long must downloaded tachograph data be kept?
faqs.a: Article 10(5) of Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 requires downloaded vehicle unit and driver card data to be kept for at least 12 months following recording and to be accessible on request. Article 33(2) of Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 requires record sheets and printouts to be kept for at least a year after use.
